column1:
Banking Act 2016 (Amendment):
The amendment, enacted in November
2019, repealed the interest rate capping
framework that had been in place since
September 2016.
Impact: Whilst the banking sector’s
credit portfolios as at the repeal date
will continue to be subject to the rate
caps, banks are now able to price new
credit facilities reflecting the level of risk
acquired.
Response: The Bank strongly believes on
the need to act responsibly in the pricing
of new credit in the post interest rate
capping era. It has adopted a risk- based
credit pricing model in 2020, which
enables the loan interest rates to reflect
the varying risk profiles of individual
borrowers.
